title: The Sleeping Sickness
text: Three nights ago half the city went to bed and did not wake. They breathe, turn over and smile, their eyes moving under the lids as though they are watching something together. The physicians want gold for their tinctures and grain to feed those still awake while they tend the sleepers.

temptation.label: Hire the sleepers out to the dream-readers.
temptation.text: The readers pay well to sit by the beds writing down what the sleepers say. Every sleeper says the same thing.

triumph.text: The physicians wake them one by one. Each of them says the same word on waking; none of them remember it after.

holds.text: Most wake within the month. A few never do. Their families keep them in the attic, listening to them laugh.

falters.text: The sickness reaches the Seats. One House's Scion sleeps for a season, then wakes knowing things they should not.

calamity.text: The city sleeps through a whole season. Those who stay awake keep the fires lit without looking at the sleepers' faces, which are all turned the same way: towards the Gate.
